focus.note: Many phrasal verbs are idiomatic, so the meaning cannot be guessed from the parts. Notice the particle that follows the gap, such as over, up to or on, and learn the pattern with it.

items.s: Mutual friends helped the brothers ____ up their quarrel after ten years.

speak.title: Role-play: should I go to the reunion?
speak.setup: Work in pairs. Read your card, then have the conversation. Swap roles and do it again.

a.role: the person who wants to go
a.text: A reunion for your old school class is next month. You want to go and say sorry to a classmate you did not help at school. Explain why it matters to you. Listen to your friend and decide what to do.

b.text: You think it may be a bad idea. The other person might not want to talk about the past, and a party is not the right place. Ask questions and suggest another way to say sorry.

phrases: I've been thinking about it for years.
I'd like to say sorry to him in person.
What if he doesn't want to talk about it?
That's a fair point, but I can't stay silent.
Maybe a message would be easier for him.
Let's agree that I'll ask him first.
speak.after: Afterwards, tell the class: did you decide to apologise at the reunion, and how?
